_: Things in the estate. x/y place the node in the estate view — the agent sits at the centre and everything else on an ellipse round it, so every edge is a spoke and none crosses a node. exists_facts: ANY of these puts the twin in the estate. presence_facts: the facts that ANSWER whether it is here at all — exempt from the gate, so 'no agent' renders as an edge rather than a blank screen. depends_on: it cannot be there unless that one is.

items.label: The agent
items.note: The subject. Everything else is what it touches or what governs it.

items.label: The production estate
items.note: In scope as a concept whether or not the agent is there yet. Where the agent runs changes the IMPACT of a finding, never whether the finding is true.

items.label: The data in its reach
items.note: Its CLASS is what decides whether any of the rest matters.

items.label: Decisions its output affects
items.note: Where an agent stops being infrastructure.

items.label: Its entitlements
items.note: Promoted to a node so 'we do not know what it can reach' is a visible edge rather than a silent gap.

items.label: Stop authority
items.note: Held by a person, a group, or nobody — and the third is an edge like the others.

items.label: The stop control
items.note: One node, four questions: whether it exists, how long it takes, what it takes down, and whether it has ever been used.

items.label: Test and QA environments
items.note: An agent here is real and carries almost none of the exposure. Separating it from production is what makes 'yes, but only in QA' an answer rather than a hedge.
